decisions.quote: Unlike Study 1 that measured naturally occurring response effort, Study 2 manipulated response effort on the sentence unscrambling task. Support for the cleanliness hypothesis was found among participants instructed to work through the sentence unscrambling task as quickly as possible. In contrast, when participants were instructed to work on the sentence unscrambling task attentively, no support was found for the hypothesized effect of the cleanliness priming.
decisions.reason: Across both Study 1 and Study 2, the overall unmoderated cleanliness priming effect was non-significant, with the original effect replicating only among low-effort participants and failing to hold among high-effort participants, establishing response effort as a boundary condition and yielding a mixed outcome.

decisions.quote: It should be noted that these pilot results, albeit promising, were highly exploratory, and thus should not be interpreted as confirmatory evidence. Instead, these tentative results point to the need for a comprehensive examination of the role of response effort.
decisions.reason: Johnson et al. (2014a) is an earlier replication attempt from which materials were obtained to replicate Schnall et al. (2008a) Experiment 1, and the brief mention of Pilot Study 1 refers to an exploratory subgroup analysis in the supplementary material that the author explicitly disclaims as non-confirmatory motivation rather than a central target re-test.

parent_source_inspection.note: Abstract and Study2 discussion frame effort as boundary condition, low effort explicitly still acceptable. Direct replication of original Schnall effects, not independent Johnson target; exploratory pilot motivation distinguished.
